zh.title: 阿姆斯特丹史基浦機場A區停機坪全面導入電動GPU KLM地勤作業進一步減少柴油設備使用
zh.summary: 荷蘭皇家航空（KLM）近日宣佈，其位於阿姆斯特丹史基浦機場（AMS）A 區停機坪的地面作業現已全面使用電動地面電源設備（Electric Ground Power Unit，e-GPU），取代傳統柴油式 GPU。這項轉變是史基浦機場持續推動空側地面設備電氣化的一環，目標在降低機坪作業產生的排放與噪音，並改善地勤人員的工作環境。
body: 荷蘭皇家航空（KLM）近日宣佈，其位於阿姆斯特丹史基浦機場（AMS）A 區停機坪的地面作業現已全面使用電動地面電源設備（Electric Ground Power Unit，e-GPU），取代傳統柴油式 GPU。這項轉變是史基浦機場持續推動空側地面設備電氣化的一環，目標在降低機坪作業產生的排放與噪音，並改善地勤人員的工作環境。
地面電源設備（Ground Power Unit，GPU）主要在航機停靠地面、發動機關閉期間提供外部電力，供應客艙照明、駕駛艙電腦及其他機載系統使用。若停機位沒有固定式地面電源，通常需要使用可移動式 GPU；改採電動設備後，可減少柴油發電機在航機周邊持續運轉所產生的廢氣與噪音。史基浦機場指出，外部電源亦有助於降低航機使用輔助動力系統（Auxiliary Power Unit，APU）的時間。
史基浦機場的 GPU 電氣化並非近期才開始推動。機場自 2010 年起逐步淘汰柴油 GPU，並自 2017 年與地面設備製造商 ITW 合作開發電池式 e-GPU，首批設備於 2021 年底投入使用。2023 年，史基浦機場進一步宣布引進 30 部新的 e-GPU，KLM Equipment Services 當時也表示，相關計畫與其在 2030 年以前將 GPU 設備全面電氣化的目標一致。
與固定式地面電源不同，e-GPU 本身具備移動能力，可部署在尚未建置固定供電設施或位於遠端停機坪的航機旁。史基浦機場表示，其電動 GPU 採用大型電池組供電，充電後可支援停場航機所需的地面電力；機場也持續擴充固定式 400 Hz 地面電源與預調空氣設備，以降低航機在停場期間對柴油設備及 APU 的依賴。
史基浦機場曾表示，透過擴大停場航機的電力供應，其機坪相關排放量已降低約 30%，同時可減少作業區噪音。機場與 KLM 等業者的長期目標，是在 2030 年前推動地面作業朝零排放方向發展；此次 A 區停機坪完成電氣化，則代表相關設備的部署進一步擴展至 KLM 實際地勤作業區域。

en.title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport’s A‑Area Apron Fully Adopts Electric GPUs; KLM Ground Operations Further Reduce Diesel Equipment Use
en.summary: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines recently announced that its ground operations at the A‑area apron of Amsterdam Schiphol Airport (AMS) now fully use electric ground power units (e‑GPU), replacing traditional diesel GPUs. This shift is part of Schiphol Airport’s ongoing effort to electrify airside ground equipment, aiming to cut emissions and noise from apron operations and improve the working environment for ground staff.
body: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines recently announced that its ground operations at the A‑area apron of Amsterdam Schiphol Airport (AMS) now fully use electric ground power units (e‑GPU), replacing traditional diesel GPUs. This transition is part of Schiphol Airport’s ongoing push to electrify airside ground equipment, aiming to reduce emissions and noise from apron operations and improve the working environment for ground staff.

Ground Power Units (GPUs) primarily supply external electrical power while an aircraft is parked with its engines shut down, powering cabin lighting, flight‑deck computers and other onboard systems. When a stand lacks a fixed ground‑power installation, a mobile GPU is normally required; switching to electric units cuts the exhaust and noise produced by diesel generators running continuously around the aircraft. Schiphol notes that external power also helps reduce the time aircraft need to run their Auxiliary Power Units (APUs).

Schiphol’s GPU electrification did not begin only recently. The airport started phasing out diesel GPUs in 2010 and, from 2017, partnered with ground‑equipment manufacturer ITW to develop battery‑powered e‑GPUs, with the first units entering service at the end of 2021. In 2023 Schiphol announced the acquisition of 30 additional e‑GPUs, and KLM Equipment Services stated at the time that the program aligns with its goal of fully electrifying GPU equipment by 2030.

Unlike fixed ground‑power installations, e‑GPUs are mobile and can be deployed next to aircraft at stands that lack fixed power infrastructure or on remote aprons. Schiphol says its electric GPUs use large battery packs; once charged they can supply the ground power a parked aircraft requires. The airport is also continuing to expand fixed 400 Hz ground‑power and pre‑conditioned air systems to lessen aircraft reliance on diesel equipment and APUs while on the ground.

Schiphol has previously reported that expanding electrical supply to parked aircraft has cut apron‑related emissions by roughly 30 % and also reduced noise in the operating area. The long‑term objective of the airport and partners such as KLM is to drive ground operations toward zero emissions by 2030; the completion of electrification at the A‑area apron marks a further extension of this equipment deployment into KLM’s actual ground‑handling zones.
